title: Basic-auth issue detection invoke: experiment UPDATE is not enough when a gateway secret_id is passed; also require USE on that secret
answers: Why can a user run issue detection with another user's AI Gateway secret?
What permission does POST issues/invoke need when the request includes a secret_id?
Where is the auth check for issue detection invoke handled?
If I add a route that decrypts a gateway secret taken from the request, which permission should it check?
body:
Path: mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:validate_can_invoke_issue_detection, registered for (INVOKE_ISSUE_DETECTION, POST) in BEFORE_REQUEST_VALIDATORS. It guards POST /ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/issues/invoke, the issue-detection job launch, which takes experiment_id, trace_ids, provider, model and an optional secret_id.
Rule: The validator first requires UPDATE on the request's experiment (validate_can_update_experiment). If the JSON body has a truthy secret_id, it also requires USE on that gateway secret via _get_gateway_secret_permission(secret_id).can_use, the same helper the gateway secret RPCs use. The handler (_invoke_issue_detection_handler) decrypts that secret through _fetch_provider_credentials, so any route that passes a caller-supplied secret id to credential fetch needs this USE check.
Symptom: Any user with UPDATE on their own experiment could make the server decrypt and use another user's AI Gateway secret, with the plaintext provider key injected into the job environment.
Constraints: An absent or empty secret_id skips the secret check, matching the handler's `if secret_id:`; do not switch to `is None` or the request is 403ed for a value the handler treats as no secret. Unknown secret ids resolve to no grant and are denied, so the route is not an existence oracle. genai/evaluate/invoke and scorer/invoke take no secret_id and keep only the experiment check. An endpoint_name on the same route is not checked against endpoint permissions (known gap).
applies: Basic-auth server authorization for issue-detection invoke and any route that uses a caller-supplied gateway secret id; not for the gateway secret CRUD routes or the evaluate/scorer invoke routes.
says: Running issue detection allows members to use another person's saved gateway credentials.
Users can trigger trace issue scans using private AI gateway keys without permission.
Require access rights on the selected gateway secret when launching issue detection jobs.
Prevent team members from running automated issue detection with credentials they cannot use.
search: For POST /ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/issues/invoke, mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:validate_can_invoke_issue_detection requires UPDATE on the experiment and checks USE via _get_gateway_secret_permission(secret_id).can_use when a truthy secret_id is present. Any route decrypting a caller-supplied secret via _fetch_provider_credentials must perform this USE check, whereas empty or absent secret_id values skip it and unknown IDs are denied. Scorer and evaluation invoke routes do not accept secret_id, and endpoint_name on this route is not checked against endpoint permissions.
